transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-19
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (LynxData CTO), Miguel Santos (LynxData ML Eng), Evelyn Zhou (LynxData Security)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand LynxData's planned exit from an internal vLLM/TGI stack and evaluate hosting options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Key concerns: eval parity with current vLLM/TGI results, latency & cost tradeoffs, KMS/encryption and audit logs, and timeline for a pilot/POC.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and pain points (vLLM + TGI orchestration)
- Performance parity and benchmarks
- Networking and security requirements (VPC, SSO, KMS/HSM, SOC2)
- Rollout/rollback strategy and canary testing
- Pricing and committed capacity vs burst options
- Next steps: benchmark, security packet, pricing sheet, pilot SOW

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): alright everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Alex Morales from Redwood, AE. Jordan Kim, our solutions engineer, will take the deep technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya (CTO): good thanks, morning for us, afternoon there. Quick context: we've been running an in-house vLLM orchestrated stack with TGI for a year, trying to reduce spend and simplify ops. We're exploring an exit to a managed option but we have strict latency SLOs for our inference pipeline.
[00:22] Miguel (ML Eng): yeah, to add — our 95th percentile is sub-300ms for shorter prompts, and we see tokenized convs up to 1.2k tokens. We've tuned kv cache and batching heavily.
[00:35] Jordan (SE): okay great. Just to align, when you say vLLM + TGI, are you using a particular quantized model variants or more fp16? and what's your deployment topology — single AZ or multi-AZ?
[00:46] Miguel: we run mostly int8 quant on A100s, multi-AZ in GCP, with a small private network. We have hot KV cache in memory — that's a big part of latency.
[00:58] Priya: also need to call out compliance — SOC2 type II, SSO via SAML, and we need KMS/HSM integration for model keys and dataset encryption.
[01:10] Alex: perfect, all items Redwood supports across Dedicated and Private modes. I'll hand to Jordan to walk through the parity and routing story.
[01:17] Jordan: thanks. High level — we do three flavors: Hosted (fastest onboarding), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For parity with vLLM/TGI we look at kernel selection, kv cache semantics, and quantization path. Our Dedicated nodes can run int8 profiles and we have a prefix/KV caching layer to match your hot-cache behavior.
[01:38] Miguel: quick question — vllm allows custom attention hooks we rely on for a couple of model optimizations, will Redwood preserve those or are there limitations?
[01:47] Jordan: good question. We support common attention optimizations and can surface hooks via our runtime, but custom native vLLM hooks may need porting. In practice, we replicate the effect with our optimized kernels; sometimes small code changes in the model wrapper are required. We can include that in the POC to validate parity.
[02:05] Evelyn (Security): can you talk about audit logs and retention? we have regulatory needs to keep request/response metadata for 1 year.
[02:13] Alex: we offer token-level logging and configurable retention on Dedicated and Private. Hosted also supports logs but retention windows differ — we'd share the security packet with exact SLAs. We'll note 1-year requirement.
[02:25] Priya: cost — our CFO is wary of per-token surprises. We want predictable economics; dedicated reserved capacity looks interesting but we need burst behavior during launches.
[02:36] Alex: yes reserved capacity for steady throughput plus burst lanes is standard. We'll model your current token usage and show cost vs latency curves — that'll be in the spreadsheet.
[02:45] Miguel: benchmarking — we ran TGI inference with a mix of short and long contexts; can Redwood run our prompt set to compare wall-clock and token cost?
[02:55] Jordan: absolutely. We generally do a benchmark window on Dedicated to mirror your infra, run your prompt set, and produce per-prompt latency, p95, memory profiles, and token cost. If you want, we can run a Hosted quick test first for a smoke check.
[03:09] Priya: timeline — we need something in staging in 3 weeks and a pilot in 6. feasible?
[03:15] Alex: feasible. Proposed path: 1) share prompt set + telemetry (you) 2) Redwood runs baseline Hosted smoke & Dedicated benchmark (Jordan) 3) review results and decide Dedicated reserved vs Private (security review) 4) pilot SOW. We can align dates after the spreadsheet.
[03:29] Miguel: about the prefix/KV behavior — our cache returns are sometimes slightly different in tokenization boundaries, that led to 10–15ms delta. How precise is your cache behavior?
[03:40] Jordan: our KV cache is sequence-aware; we replicate internal keying used by the model runtime. There can be micro-diffs from vLLM, but functionally we aim to keep token-by-token parity. We'll include debug traces in the benchmark.
[03:53] Evelyn: SSO and RBAC: we need SCIM provisioning and attribute-based access — can Redwood integrate with our Okta?
[03:59] Alex: yes SAML + SCIM + RBAC supported on enterprise accounts. We'll include a short integration doc.
[04:07] Priya: encryption at rest and in transit — KMS tie-in is mandatory, ideally customer-managed keys.
[04:13] Jordan: customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM is available in Private and Dedicated (with private control plane option). Hosted also supports CMEK for enterprise tiers; we'll clarify specifics in the security packet.
[04:26] Miguel: curious on rollback/rollout — we have a canary flow and require automatic fallback to a smaller model if big regression happens.
[04:34] Jordan: Redwood supports rollouts (canary + A/B) and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants. You can pin model versions and set automatic rollback thresholds tied to eval metrics.
[04:47] Priya: eval metrics — we use an open prompt suite and human eval for a subset; can you run quality regression checks?
[04:54] Alex: yes, our Optimize product can run prompt-based quality checks and alert on regressions. For the POC we'd run both perf and quality parity.
[05:02] Miguel: small nit: our ops uses a custom header and tracing — do you preserve trace headers end-to-end?
[05:09] Jordan: yes we preserve custom request headers and support tracing hooks. We'll add an example.
[05:15] Priya: great. any known incompatibilities with TGI-specific plugins?
[05:20] Jordan: some vendor-specific TGI plugins might not be 1:1; we usually map or reimplement critical ones during the POC.
[05:28] Alex: sounds like next steps are clear. We'll send the cost/latency sheet, security packet, and propose benchmark windows. Jordan will own the benchmark runbook.
[05:36] Priya: can we get an NDA/contract template earlier? legal will review the SOW.
[05:41] Alex: yes we'll share standard enterprise NDA and SOW templates; legal will follow up with your counsel.
[05:46] Evelyn: one more — data residency: our EU customers' data must stay in EU regions. Is region pinning supported?
[05:53] Jordan: yes region-aware routing and dedicated clusters in EU available for Dedicated or Private. We'll mark that in the proposal.
[05:59] Priya: perfect. we'll send prompt set and telemetry by Friday.
[06:03] Alex: thanks everyone. We'll recap via email and include links: benchmark playbook (link), cost sheet (link), security packet (link), and scheduling form for benchmark windows.

References shared: benchmark-playbook: https://redwood.test/playbooks/lynx-benchmark (placeholder), cost-model-sheet: https://redwood.test/sheets/lynx-costs, security-packet: https://redwood.test/security/enterprise-packet.pdf
